claim: Ovarian surface epithelium (OSE) undergoes recurring ovulatory rupture.
source: Ovarian surface epithelium (OSE) undergoes recurring ovulatory rupture and OSE stem cells rapidly generate new cells for the repair.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature (Gaytán et al., 2005; Auersperg et al., 2001) in the Introduction section.

claim: OSE stem cells rapidly generate new cells for repair after ovulatory rupture.
source: Ovarian surface epithelium (OSE) undergoes recurring ovulatory rupture and OSE stem cells rapidly generate new cells for the repair.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature and the study's own findings.

claim: Protein C Receptor (Procr) marks OSE progenitors.
source: Our previous study has identified that Protein C Receptor (Procr) marks OSE progenitors.
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study (Wang et al., 2019).

claim: Adherent junction is decreased at the OSE rupture site.
source: In this study, we observed decreased adherent junction and selective activation of YAP signaling in Procr progenitors at OSE rupture site.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data showing decreased E-cadherin, α-catenin, and ZO-1 at rupture sites (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: YAP signaling is selectively activated in Procr progenitors at OSE rupture site.
source: In this study, we observed decreased adherent junction and selective activation of YAP signaling in Procr progenitors at OSE rupture site.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining and in situ hybridization data showing nuclear Yap1 and Ccn1 expression in Procr+ cells at rupture sites (Figure 1E-J).

claim: OSE repair is impeded upon deletion of Yap1 in Procr progenitors.
source: OSE repair is impeded upon deletion of Yap1 in these progenitors.
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data showing delayed repair in Yap1-cKO mice (Figure 2B-E).

claim: Procr+ progenitors show lower expression of Vgll4 compared to Procr- cells.
source: Interestingly, Procr+ progenitors show lower expression of Vgll4, an antagonist of YAP signaling.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and immunostaining data (Figure 3A-E).

claim: Vgll4 is an antagonist of YAP signaling.
source: Interestingly, Procr+ progenitors show lower expression of Vgll4, an antagonist of YAP signaling.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature (Chen et al., 2004; Feng et al., 2019).

claim: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cells hampers OSE repair.
source: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cells hampers OSE repair and progenitor proliferation, indicating that selective low Vgll4 expression in Procr+ progenitors is critical for OSE repair.
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data showing delayed repair in Vgll4-OE mice (Figure 3I-L).

claim: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cells hampers progenitor proliferation.
source: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cells hampers OSE repair and progenitor proliferation, indicating that selective low Vgll4 expression in Procr+ progenitors is critical for OSE repair.
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation and colony formation assays (Figure 3M-R).

claim: Selective low Vgll4 expression in Procr+ progenitors is critical for OSE repair.
source: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cells hampers OSE repair and progenitor proliferation, indicating that selective low Vgll4 expression in Procr+ progenitors is critical for OSE repair.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental results showing impaired repair when Vgll4 is overexpressed.

claim: YAP activation promotes transcription of the OSE stemness gene Procr.
source: In addition, YAP activation promotes transcription of the OSE stemness gene Procr.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR and luciferase reporter assays (Figure 4J-M).

claim: The combination of increased cell division and Procr expression leads to expansion of Procr+ progenitors surrounding the rupture site.
source: The combination of increased cell division and Procr expression leads to expansion of Procr+ progenitors surrounding the rupture site.
evidence: Supported by FACS analysis and imaging data showing increased Procr+ cell numbers at rupture sites (Figure 4A-I).

claim: After ovulation, the wound is completely closed within 12 hr to 3 days following rupture.
source: After ovulation, to maintain the physiological function and morphology of the ovary, the wound is completely closed within 12 hr to 3 days following rupture (Burdette et al., 2006; Ng and Barker, 2015; Tan and Fleming, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cells surrounding the damaged sites respond to the wound by turning on cell proliferation.
source: Cells surrounding the damaged sites are required to respond to the wound by turning on cell proliferation to supply sufficient cells as building blocks for regeneration (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Procr+ OSE stem/progenitor cells are the major contributor for ovulatory rupture repair.
source: Our previous study has identified that Procr+ OSE stem/progenitor cells are the major contributor for ovulatory rupture repair.
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study (Wang et al., 2019).

claim: Targeted ablation of Procr+ cells hampers OSE repair.
source: Targeted ablation of these cells hampers the repair (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study.

claim: Procr+ cells expand instantly upon ovulation.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Procr+ cells expand instantly upon ovulation, reminiscent of a result of symmetric division (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study.

claim: E-cadherin expression is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture compared to other regions.
source: Interestingly, we found that E-cadherin, α-catenin, and ZO-1 staining is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture (defined as within 20 cells on one side of the rupture in section) compared to other regions, that is, rupture distal region (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and nonrupture region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: α-catenin staining is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture compared to other regions.
source: Interestingly, we found that E-cadherin, α-catenin, and ZO-1 staining is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture (defined as within 20 cells on one side of the rupture in section) compared to other regions, that is, rupture distal region (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and nonrupture region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ZO-1 staining is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture compared to other regions.
source: Interestingly, we found that E-cadherin, α-catenin, and ZO-1 staining is markedly decreased at the proximal region of rupture (defined as within 20 cells on one side of the rupture in section) compared to other regions, that is, rupture distal region (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and nonrupture region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Adherent junction has been implicated as a modulator of YAP signaling.
source: As adherent junction has been implicated as a modulator of YAP signaling (Kim et al., 2011; Schlegelmilch et al., 2011; Varelas et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015), we examined YAP activities at the rupture area by immunostaining.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There is an increased incidence of nuclear Yap1 at the proximal region of rupture compared to other regions.
source: We observed an increased incidence of nuclear Yap1 at the proximal region of rupture compared to other regions (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: Compromised adherent junctions resulting from ovulatory rupture are associated with Yap1 nuclear localization in OSE cells surrounding the wound.
source: These results suggest that compromised adherent junctions resulting from ovulatory rupture are associated with Yap1 nuclear localization in OSE cells surrounding the wound.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between decreased adherent junction proteins and increased nuclear Yap1.

claim: Procr+ cells at the rupture proximal region have significantly higher nuclear Yap1 staining (75.9% ± 1.7%) compared to Procr− cells (39.6% ± 1.0%).
source: We found that Procr+ (H2B-GFP+) cells at the rupture proximal region (referred to as rupture site from here on) have significantly higher nuclear Yap1 staining (75.9% ± 1.7%) compared to Procr− cells (39.6% ± 1.0%) (Figure 1E, G), or compared to Procr+ cells at the nonrupture region (Figure 1F, G).
evidence: Supported by quantification of immunostaining data shown in Figure 1E, G.

claim: At the rupture site, Ccn1 is preferentially activated in Procr+ OSE cells, with 44.8% ± 2.9% of Procr+ cells being Ccn1+, which is markedly higher than that of Procr− cells (8.9% ± 0.8%).
source: We found that, at the rupture site, Ccn1 is preferentially activated in Procr+ OSE cells, with 44.8% ± 2.9% of Procr+ cells being Ccn1+, which is markedly higher than that of Procr− cells (8.9% ± 0.8%) (Figure 1H, J).
evidence: Supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1H, J.

claim: Procr+ cells at rupture sites have a higher level of Birc5 expression compared to Procr− cells.
source: qPCR analysis indicated that Procr+ cells at rupture sites have a higher level of Birc5 expression compared to Procr− cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: YAP signaling was specifically activated in Procr+ cells at the rupture site.
source: Together, these results suggest that YAP signaling was specifically activated in Procr+ cells at the rupture site.
evidence: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence including nuclear Yap1, Ccn1 expression, and Birc5 expression in Procr+ cells.

claim: Only Procr+, but not Procr−, cells at the rupture site displayed increased proliferation.
source: Considering the role of YAP signaling in promoting cell proliferation, these results are in line with our previous observations that only Procr+, but not Procr−, cells at the rupture site displayed increased proliferation (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study.

claim: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), Ctrl and Yap1-cKO ovaries had similar ruptures.
source: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the two groups had similar ruptures (Figure 2B, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 2B, E.

claim: At 6 dpi, Ctrl ovaries underwent rapid repairing.
source: At 6 dpi, Ctrl ovaries underwent rapid repairing (Figure 2C, E), and the OSE was completely recovered by 7.5 dpi (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 2C, E.

claim: The OSE in Ctrl ovaries was completely recovered by 7.5 dpi.
source: At 6 dpi, Ctrl ovaries underwent rapid repairing (Figure 2C, E), and the OSE was completely recovered by 7.5 dpi (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 2D, E.

claim: The OSE repair in Yap1-cKO ovaries was significantly delayed at both 6 and 7.5 dpi.
source: In contrast, the OSE repair in Yap1-cKO ovaries was significantly delayed at both 6 and 7.5 dpi (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 2C-E.

claim: The number of proliferating OSE cells at rupture site was significantly decreased from 5.5 ± 0.3 EdU+ in Ctrl to 1.4 ± 0.2 EdU+ in Yap1-cKO at 4.5 dpi (ovulation).
source: When analyzed at 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the number of proliferating OSE cells at rupture site (defined as 20 cells on one side from the opening) was significantly decreased from 5.5 ± 0.3 EdU+ in Ctrl to 1.4 ± 0.2 EdU+ in Yap1-cKO (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 2F-H.

claim: Deletion of Yap1 in Procr+ cells drastically inhibited OSE colony formation in vitro.
source: Deletion of Yap1 in Procr+ cells drastically inhibited OSE colony formation (Figure 2J, K).
evidence: Supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 2J, K.

claim: At 4.5 dpi, control ovary displayed a zone of mGFP+ cells that are the progeny of Procr+ progenitors surrounding the rupture sites.
source: At 4.5 dpi, control (Procr-CreER;R26-mTmG) ovary displayed a zone of mGFP+ cells that are the progeny of Procr+ progenitors surrounding the rupture sites (Figure 2M).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Yap1-cKO ovaries have markedly fewer mGFP+ cells around the wound at 4.5 dpi.
source: In contrast, Yap1-cKO (Procr-CreER;Yap1fl/fl;R26-mTmG) ovaries have markedly fewer mGFP+ cells around the wound (Figure 2M, O), supporting the notion that the activity of Procr+ progenitors was hampered at the beginning of the repairing process.
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2M, O.

claim: At 7 dpi, control ovaries had generated patches of mGFP+ cells covering the newly formed corpus luteum.
source: At 7 dpi, control ovaries had generated patches of mGFP+ cells covering the newly formed corpus luteum (Figure 2N).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2N.

claim: Yap1-cKO ovaries still had obvious openings with few mGFP+ cells at 7 dpi.
source: However, Yap1-cKO ovaries still had obvious openings with few mGFP+ cells (Figure 2N, O).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2N, O.

claim: YAP signaling activation is crucial for the proliferation of Procr+ progenitor cells and the timely repair of OSE after rupture.
source: Together, these results suggest that YAP signaling activation is crucial for the proliferation of Procr+ progenitor cells and the timely repair of OSE after rupture.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing impaired proliferation and repair when Yap1 is deleted.

claim: Vgll4 is a negative regulator of YAP by inhibiting the binding of YAP and TEAD4.
source: Vgll4 is a negative regulator of YAP by inhibiting the binding of YAP and TEAD4 (Feng et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Procr+ cells have lower level of Vgll4 compared to Procr− cells at the rupture sites.
source: qPCR analysis indicated that Procr+ cells have lower level of Vgll4 compared to Procr− cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Procr+ cells exhibited lower Vgll4 protein expression compared to Procr− cells.
source: Consistent with the qPCR results, Procr+ cells also exhibited lower Vgll4 protein expression compared to Procr− cells (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: The rupture in Ctrl and Vgll4-OE ovaries are comparable at 4.5 dpi.
source: We found that the rupture in Ctrl and Vgll4-OE ovaries are comparable at 4.5 dpi (Figure 3I, L).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 3I, L.

claim: At 6 dpi, while Ctrl ovaries had sights of wound closure, Vgll4-OE ovaries still showed larger areas of rupture.
source: At 6 dpi, while Ctrl ovaries had sights of wound closure, Vgll4-OE ovaries still showed larger areas of rupture (Figure 3J, L).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 3J, L.

claim: At 7.5 dpi, Ctrl ovaries displayed complete OSE, whereas the repair in Vgll4-OE ovaries was obviously delayed.
source: At 7.5 dpi, Ctrl ovaries displayed complete OSE, whereas the repair in Vgll4-OE ovaries was obviously delayed (Figure 3K, L).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 3K, L.

claim: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the number of proliferating OSE cells at rupture site was significantly decreased from 3.7 ± 0.3 in Ctrl to 1.0 ± 0.2 in Vgll4-OE.
source: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the number of proliferating OSE cells at rupture site was significantly decreased from 3.7 ± 0.3 in Ctrl to 1.0 ± 0.2 in Vgll4-OE (Figure 3M–O).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 3M-O.

claim: Overexpression of Vgll4 inhibits cell proliferation and colony formation in vitro.
source: Consistently, overexpression of Vgll4 inhibits cell proliferation and colony formation (Figure 3Q, R).
evidence: Supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3Q, R.

claim: Overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cell impaired Procr+ cell proliferation and ovulatory rupture repair.
source: Together, these results suggest that overexpression of Vgll4 in Procr+ cell impaired Procr+ cell proliferation and ovulatory rupture repair.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing impaired proliferation and repair when Vgll4 is overexpressed.

claim: Procr+ progenitor cells expand instantly at the periphery of the rupture site upon ovulation.
source: We have previously found that Procr+ progenitor cells expand instantly at the periphery of the rupture site upon ovulation (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous study.

claim: FACS analysis showed a dramatic decrease of Procr+ progenitor population when Yap1 was deleted at 4.5 dpi (ovulation).
source: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), FACS analysis showed a dramatic decrease of Procr+ progenitor population when Yap1 was deleted (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: At the wound edge of control ovary at 4.5 dpi (ovulation), there were about 7.4 ± 0.3 H2B-GFP+ cells expressing the peak level of GFP.
source: When analyzed at 4.5 dpi (ovulation), at the wound edge (defined as 20 cells on one side from the opening) of control ovary (Procr-rtTA;TetO-H2B-GFP+/−), there were about 7.4 ± 0.3 H2B-GFP+ cells expressing the peak level of GFP (Figure 4E, G).
evidence: Supported by imaging and quantification data shown in Figure 4E, G.

claim: In Vgll4-OE ovary, only 2.4 ± 0.2 H2B-GFP+ cells were observed at the wound edge at 4.5 dpi (ovulation).
source: In contrast, in Vgll4-OE ovary (Procr-rtTA;TetO-Vgll4;TetO-H2B-GFP+/−), only 2.4 ± 0.2 H2B-GFP+ cells were observed at the wound edge (Figure 4F, G).
evidence: Supported by imaging and quantification data shown in Figure 4F, G.

claim: The percentage of Procr+ progenitor population decreased significantly from 18.5% ± 1.0% in Ctrl to 7.4% ± 1.2% in Vgll4-OE at ovulation stage.
source: FACS analysis also showed that the percentage of Procr+ progenitor population decreased significantly from 18.5% ± 1.0% in Ctrl to 7.4% ± 1.2% in Vgll4-OE at ovulation stage (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 4H, I.

claim: In control cells, frequent division of Procr+ cells was observed, and in most cases, it was one Procr+ cell dividing into two Procr+ cells.
source: In control cells, we observed frequent division of Procr+ cells, and in most cases, it was one Procr+ cell dividing into two Procr+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, C).
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, C.

claim: In Vgll4-OE cells, cell division could hardly be observed.
source: But in Vgll4-OE, we could hardly observe cell division (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Inhibition of YAP signaling, by either Yap1-deletion or Vgll4-OE, impairs the expansion of Procr+ progenitors upon rupture.
source: Together, these results suggest that inhibition of YAP signaling, by either Yap1-deletion or Vgll4-OE, impairs the expansion of Procr+ progenitors upon rupture.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing reduced Procr+ cell numbers when YAP signaling is inhibited.

claim: In soft condition, Yap1 was mostly cytoplasmic and most OSE cells are H2B-GFP−.
source: Consistent with the notion, we found that, in soft condition, Yap1 was mostly cytoplasmic and most OSE cells are H2B-GFP− (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Most OSE cells are H2B-GFP+ in stiff condition and Yap1 was found in the nucleus.
source: In contrast, most OSE cells are H2B-GFP+ in stiff condition and Yap1 was found in the nucleus (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: YAP activation induces Procr expression.
source: These observations suggest that YAP activation might induce Procr expression. We verified by qPCR that Procr expression is upregulated in stiff conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Knocking down Yap1 by shRNA in OSE culture inhibits Procr expression.
source: To further investigate whether Yap1 regulates Procr expression, we knocked down Yap1 by shRNA in OSE culture and found that this inhibits Procr expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D, E.

claim: Blocking YAP activation by Verteporfin (VP) resulted in lower Procr expression.
source: Furthermore, blocking YAP activation by Verteporfin (VP) or Vgll4 overexpression also resulted in lower Procr expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Vgll4 overexpression resulted in lower Procr expression.
source: Furthermore, blocking YAP activation by Verteporfin (VP) or Vgll4 overexpression also resulted in lower Procr expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2G.

claim: Inhibiting YAP signaling suppresses Procr expression.
source: These results suggest that inhibiting YAP signaling suppresses Procr expression.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing reduced Procr expression when YAP signaling is inhibited.

claim: A Tead4-binding motif (5′-CATTCC-3′) was found at the proximal promoter of Procr (−1486 to −1481 bp).
source: A Tead4-binding motif (5′-CATTCC-3′) was found at the proximal promoter of Procr (−1486 to −1481 bp) (Figure 4J).
evidence: Supported by promoter analysis shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Tead4 could directly bind to the Procr promoter.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation-qPCR (ChIP-qPCR) showed that Tead4 could directly bind to the Procr promoter (Figure 4K).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Yap1 induced the wild-type Procr promoter luciferase in a dose-dependent manner.
source: While Yap1 induced the wild-type promoter luciferase in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4L and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I), it could not activate the mutant reporter with the deletion of the Tead4-binding motif (Figure 4M and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I).
evidence: Supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4L and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I.

claim: Yap1 could not activate the mutant Procr promoter reporter with the deletion of the Tead4-binding motif.
source: While Yap1 induced the wild-type promoter luciferase in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4L and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I), it could not activate the mutant reporter with the deletion of the Tead4-binding motif (Figure 4M and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I).
evidence: Supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4M and Figure 4—figure supplement 2H, I.

claim: Yap1 directly promotes Procr expression.
source: These results suggest that Yap1 directly promotes Procr expression.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assay results showing direct binding and transcriptional activation.

claim: YAP signaling promotes expansion of Procr+ cells at rupture site through a combination of increased cell division and Procr expression.
source: Together, our data support a model that YAP signaling promotes expansion of Procr+ cells at rupture site through a combination of increased cell division and Procr expression (Figure 4N).
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results and summarized in the model shown in Figure 4N.

claim: Ctrl and Procr-cKO ovaries formed comparable ruptures at 4.5 dpi (ovulation).
source: Ctrl and Procr-cKO ovaries formed comparable ruptures at 4.5 dpi (ovulation) (Figure 5B, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 5B, E.

claim: At 6 dpi (OSE repair ongoing), control ovaries showed smaller openings compared to Procr-cKO.
source: At 6 dpi (OSE repair ongoing), control ovaries showed smaller openings compared to Procr-cKO (Figure 5C, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 5C, E.

claim: At 7.5 dpi (OSE repair completed), Ctrl ovaries were covered by complete OSE, whereas Procr-cKO ovaries still had regions with unrepaired OSE.
source: At 7.5 dpi (OSE repair completed), Ctrl ovaries were covered by complete OSE, whereas Procr-cKO ovaries still had regions with unrepaired OSE (Figure 5D, E).
evidence: Supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 5D, E.

claim: At 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the number of proliferated OSE cells at rupture site decreased from 4.7 ± 0.4 cells in control to 1.6 ± 0.2 cells in Procr-cKO.
source: Furthermore, at 4.5 dpi (ovulation), the ovaries were harvested after 12 hr of EdU incorporation. The number of proliferated OSE cells at rupture site decreased from 4.7 ± 0.4 cells in control (Procrfl/+) to 1.6 ± 0.2 cells in Procr-cKO (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: Deletion of Procr inhibits the proliferation of progenitor cells, resulting in reduced colony sizes in vitro.
source: We found that deletion of Procr inhibits the proliferation of progenitor cells, resulting in reduced colony sizes (Figure 5J–L).
evidence: Supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 5J-L.

claim: Procr is essential for progenitor property upon rupture.
source: Overall, these data suggest that Procr is essential for progenitor property upon rupture.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing impaired proliferation and repair when Procr is deleted.

claim: YAP (Yes-associated protein, also known as YAP1) signaling is an evolutionarily conserved pathway and a master regulator of organ size and tissue growth during animal development.
source: YAP (Yes-associated protein, also known as YAP1) signaling is an evolutionarily conserved pathway and a master regulator of organ size and tissue growth during animal development (Moya and Halder, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: YAP is critical for regeneration in different organs, through triggering cell proliferation, cell survival, or expansion of stem and progenitor cell compartments.
source: As a downstream effector, YAP is critical for regeneration in different organs, through triggering cell proliferation, cell survival, or expansion of stem and progenitor cell compartments (Johnson and Halder, 2014; Lin et al., 2017b; Moya and Halder, 2016; Panciera et al., 2016; Patel et al., 2017; Xiao et al., 2016; Zhang and Del Re, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: YAP is a transcriptional coactivator protein that shuttles between the cytoplasm and nucleus.
source: YAP is a transcriptional coactivator protein that shuttles between the cytoplasm and nucleus, and regulates the expression of target genes, such as Ccn1 and Birc5, through binding with TEAD transcription factors (Chen et al., 2001; Lin et al., 2017a; Piccolo et al., 2014; Totaro et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: YAP regulates the expression of target genes, such as Ccn1 and Birc5, through binding with TEAD transcription factors.
source: YAP is a transcriptional coactivator protein that shuttles between the cytoplasm and nucleus, and regulates the expression of target genes, such as Ccn1 and Birc5, through binding with TEAD transcription factors (Chen et al., 2001; Lin et al., 2017a; Piccolo et al., 2014; Totaro et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Vgll4 serves as a transcriptional repressor of YAP through direct interactions with TEADs.
source: Vgll4, a member of Vestigial-like proteins, serves as a transcriptional repressor of YAP through direct interactions with TEADs (Chen et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Vgll4 plays important roles during development and regeneration in various tissues.
source: Previous studies from us and others have demonstrated the important roles of Vgll4 plays during development and regeneration in various tissues (Feng et al., 2019; Suo et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cell–cell junctions links cells to each other in epithelial tissues, and is an upstream negative regulator of YAP.
source: Cell–cell junctions links cells to each other in epithelial tissues, and is an upstream negative regulator of YAP (Ramos and Camargo, 2012; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mechanical forces regulate cell–cell adhesion stability.
source: Mechanical forces regulate cell–cell adhesion stability, and cell–cell adhesion junctions may be intrinsically weak at high forces (Pinheiro and Bellaϊche, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Cell–cell adhesion junctions may be intrinsically weak at high forces.
source: Mechanical forces regulate cell–cell adhesion stability, and cell–cell adhesion junctions may be intrinsically weak at high forces (Pinheiro and Bellaϊche, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Disruption of adherent junctions turns on YAP nuclear activities in lung stem/progenitor cells.
source: It has been shown that disruption of adherent junctions turns on YAP nuclear activities in lung stem/progenitor cells (Zhou et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Procr is regarded as a Wnt target gene from an in vitro screen in mammary stem cell culture.
source: Procr is regarded as a Wnt target gene from an in vitro screen in mammary stem cell culture (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: YAP is a novel upstream regulator of Procr.
source: In this study, we identify YAP as a novel upstream regulator of Procr.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assay data showing direct regulation.

claim: Procr transcription can be directly upregulated by YAP activation.
source: ChIP-qPCR and promoter luciferase experiments demonstrate that Procr transcription can be directly upregulated by YAP activation.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assay data.

claim: The phenomena of YAP promoting stem/progenitor cell expansion have been reported in various tissues.
source: The phenomena of YAP promoting stem/progenitor cell expansion have been reported in various tissues (Beverdam et al., 2013; Camargo et al., 2007; Cao et al., 2008; Ramos and Camargo, 2012; Schlegelmilch et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: This is the first report illustrating a mechanism through which YAP promotes cell proliferation, and simultaneously upregulates the expression of an essential stemness gene to maintain cell fate, leading to a rapid expansion of stem cell numbers around the wound.
